name: Portsmouth Square — deck, pagodas and the skybridge to the Hilton
note: docs/SKYPARKS.md, 'Portsmouth Square' section; skybridge rebuilt in full per BUGS.md #173 (2026-09-24). The square is the roof of Portsmouth Square Garage (OSM relation 14547583). Deck ring hand-built inside src/render/landmarks/sf/portsmouth.ts from that relation's real outer way (Overpass cache overpass-a049f7a75351625b.json), converted to local metres about this lat/lon, not from this bounding size — size/rotateDeg here only bound the placement footprint. Walter U Lum Place (the square's west edge) is at grade: the deck's edge treatment omits a retaining wall there deliberately, so a rider gets level access with no stair. Two pagoda pavilions and the Hilton skybridge (built in full — a wide brick-paved plaza-walkway with parapets, benches and gold lantern piers, a tiled gate at each end, and a stair down to the Chinese Culture Center's entrance between the Hilton's own splayed legs; not wired into the ride graph, since it dead-ends into a building interior) are built here too, since they stand ON the deck; the Empress of China is a separate entry below because it is an ordinary building beside the square, not part of the deck.

name: Empress of China
note: docs/SKYPARKS.md. Cream concrete building on Grant Ave, just across Walter U Lum Place from the square (real address 838 Grant Ave; no OSM building way for it was found in the cached Overpass extracts, so this is a standalone entry placed by hand from the aerials (ports-3/ports-4 in docs/shots/refs/aerials/), not a baked footprint — flagged per BUGS.md #146 in case a real footprint turns up later. Distinguished by large circular openings punched through the balcony slabs, storey after storey, plus the roof-garden restaurant sign across the top; both hand-built in portsmouth.ts since facade()'s notch only does rectangular bites.
